# Excellence 2026: Operational Efficiency Solutions


November 02, 2026


by Craig Patton


##


Operational efficiency has always been a priority in government, but today’s pressures are raising the stakes. Budget constraints, workforce shortages, and growing expectations for accessible, responsive services are challenging public-sector organizations to make the most of their time, people, and resources.


Technology can help by simplifying workflows, reducing manual effort, connecting processes, and giving public-sector employees more capacity to focus on the work that serves their communities. Whether through automation, cloud technology, or more connected systems, the goal is the same: make government work better for the people who depend on it.


## Celebrating Excellence in Operational Efficiency Solutions


The[Tyler Excellence Awards](https://www.tylertech.com/about-us/tyler-client-difference/tyler-excellence-awards) recognize organizations putting that principle into practice. As 2026 winds down, we’re highlighting this year’s Operational Efficiency winners — public-sector organizations using technology to remove barriers, improve essential processes, and deliver more responsive service.


## Transforming Permitting Operations for a More Responsive Experience


[New Hanover County, North Carolina](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/from-backlogs-to-one-day-setup-permitting-reimagined) , modernized their permitting process to save staff time, eliminate manual tasks, reduce delays, and rebuild community trust. The county leveraged Enterprise Permitting & Licensing to streamline communication and improve service. Improvements include:


- Reduced annual call volume by 46% through automated communications
- Cut permit setup times from 7-11 days to one day
- Reduced incomplete or incorrect submittals and cut revision time by 29% for commercial and 40% for residential projects


“What we’ve built over the last two years shows what is possible when you combine the right technology with a willingness to rethink your processes. We’ve been able to use Tyler’s software in ways that have significantly improved our workload, our team’s morale, and the experience we provide our community,” said JD Limberger, permitting director.


## Unifying Payments to Simplify and Improve Operations


In response to fragmented payment systems and reliance on external vendors, the city of[Melbourne, Florida](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/melbourne-improves-customer-experience-with-payments) , implemented a unified revenue collection solution to reduce delays, improve cash flow visibility, and support better service. Their use of the solution has:


- Reduced annual third-party processing fees by approximately $45,000
- Decreased payment processing time and improved transparency with residents
- Empowered staff with tools and knowledge to innovate across departments


“Our biggest win is the customer experience,” said Donna McMahon, customer service manager. “They are able to see their payments right away and are able to obtain the information that they need at their fingertips.”


## Modernizing Records to Improve Public Safety Response


The police department in[Ridgeland, Mississippi](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/blog-articles/ridgeland-pd-modernizes-records-improves-response) , relied on a legacy records management system that struggled to keep up with operational needs. Their adoption of Enterprise Public Safety and Enforcement Mobile has allowed them to:


- Cut report writing time significantly, from 60+ minutes to an estimated 13 minutes per report
- Increase time for proactive policing
- Improve response times
- Digitize the traffic citation process, resulting in increased traffic enforcement capabilities


“We’re seeing clear improvements in how quickly officers can complete case reports and traffic citations and get back out into the community,” said Stephen Webb, training officer. “It’s made a real difference in our day-to-day operations.”


## Replacing Paper Workflows to Improve Court Case Processing Reliability


As the caseload surged,[Medford Municipal Court, Oregon](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/medford-municipal-court-a-government-people-can-count-on) , staff recognized traditional, paper-based processes were no longer sustainable. To maintain accuracy, timeliness, and public access, the court adopted a more modern case processing workflow. Through their use of Municipal Justice, the court has:


- Improved case processing times with digital and automated workflows for every step
- Reduced case backlogs, allowing time for higher-value tasks
- Granted transparency through online public access


“We shifted from time spent on paperwork to time spent serving people,” said Cassie Neahr, municipal court supervisor. “Because of automation, we’re confident we can deliver reliable service people can count on, no matter how much caseloads grow.”


## Collaborating to Drive Efficiency Across School Districts


To drive efficient use of School ERP Pro across member districts,[Niles Township School Treasurer](https://www.tylertech.com/resources/case-studies/collaboration-drives-efficiency-across-11-school-districts) in Illinois partnered with Tyler to standardize configurations, strengthen payroll validation, and centralize training. Since identifying and implementing operational improvements, the office has:


- Aligned payroll expenses with budgeted positions to eliminate external calculations
- Validated complex pension contributions to boost data integrity
- Created a governance mechanism to continue system optimization


The training services have been particularly impactful for boosting operational efficiency for the district. “We thought, why invest in this software if we’re not going to train our people, listen to them, and teach them how to use it properly,” said CSBO Bari Cohn.
